content.intro: Modern PHP offers stronger type declarations and language constructs for making intent explicit. Choose the narrowest useful type and use enums, attributes, and readonly design only when they model a real rule. In this lesson, focus on php references; then compare it with value assignment. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use references, copy-on-write, and memory semantics when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for References, Copy-on-Write, and Memory Semantics
content_blocks.code:
<?php
interface Notifier { public function send(string $message): string; }
final class LogNotifier implements Notifier { public function send(string $message): string { return "logged: " . $message; } }
echo (new LogNotifier())->send("ready") . PHP_EOL;
